ext_field_claudeInputs_hint.message: ! lines are typed into claude's shell mode so they really run as commands — consecutive ones go in as a single line joined with ;, each behind a banner. On Warp that typing needs the Accessibility permission. A single plain-text input, with nothing else in the list, skips typing entirely and becomes claude's opening message — that additionally needs the command to end in a bare claude.

ext_migration_v1_customNote.message: This command was edited, so it is left exactly as it is — z {repo} is not its first clause, and rewriting it safely would mean parsing the shell. Replace the leading jump with {cd} yourself if you want the same fallbacks.

ext_migration_v1_describe.message: The command opens with {cd} instead of z {repo}. {cd} jumps with zoxide only to a folder named exactly like the repository, where z could also land in a worktree whose name merely contains it. If you have set a repository base folder in the Terminal Checkout app, a failed jump now falls back to that folder and clones the repository when it is not there.

ext_migration_v1_prefixDescribe.message: Your command continues after the jump. The jump now lands only in a folder named exactly like the repository, and with a base folder set, a failed jump lands in the repository folder underneath it, or in a fresh clone — make sure the rest of this command is safe to run there before accepting it.

ext_migration_v2_describe.message: This generation adds separate buttons for PR and issue list pages; existing commands are not rewritten.

ext_migration_v3_describe.message: The list pages renamed {pr}/{issue} to the {number} the detail pages already use; a saved list button still holding the old names would stop rendering.

ext_section_backup_help1.message: Settings (PR, issue, and repository buttons, and the main branch) are stored in Chrome's account-synced area (storage.sync). This extension has a fixed ID (the manifest key), so any two Chrome profiles signed in to the same Google account with "Extensions" enabled in sync settings share these settings automatically. Export and import are for moving settings without an account, or for keeping a file backup.

ext_section_backup_help2.message: Export downloads the saved settings as a file; import only fills in the form — nothing takes effect until you press $ARG1$.

ext_section_backup_help3.message: The file also records which generation of the presets it was written against. Importing an older backup offers the same update notice as stored settings do — and since a file may cover only part of your settings, the notice then reviews the whole form, not just the keys the file carried. A backup written by a newer extension is refused rather than half-read; update the extension first.

ext_section_backup_title.message: backup — export, import, account sync

ext_section_issue_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {owner} {number} (issue number, digits only) {main} — an issue has no PR branch, so the {branch} family and {base} are unavailable.

ext_section_issueList_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {owner} {number} (issue number, digits only) — a list page has no {branch} or {base}.

ext_section_main_help.message: How {main} is resolved: per-repository override → detected from the page → the default below. Detection reads the base branch on a PR page, and the repository default branch on repository and issue pages — the setting below is the fallback for when detection fails. To always use the branch a PR will actually be merged into, use {base}, which skips both the override and the default.

ext_section_pr_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — the app fills this in from its repository base folder setting, so it works on every page) {repo} {owner} {number} (PR number, digits only) {branch} (head — the branch being merged) {base} (base — the branch it merges into) {main} {branch_underbar} (branch with / replaced by _)

ext_section_prList_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {owner} {number} (PR number, digits only) — a list page has no {branch} or {base}; use gh pr checkout {number} to resolve the branch locally.

ext_section_repo_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {owner} {main} — a repository page has neither a PR or issue number nor a branch, so {number}, the {branch} family, and {base} are unavailable. {main} is resolved from the repository default branch GitHub embeds in the page — a master repository comes out right without an override.
